subject: MAP: Onramp wiring & POC infra gating — API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Onramp wiring & POC infra gating — API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Tom — following our kickoff, I pulled together a short onramp wiring plan aligned to the MAP milestones so we can close the environment gating this month. Goal: have BrightLeaf's POC environment fully reachable from our Dedicated evaluation cluster and validated by your SRE team by Oct 23.

High-level asks (owners and dates):
- Org & billing setup (BrightLeaf): create the evaluation org and invite redwood-poc@redwood.com as an admin (owner: Tom) — target: Oct 8
- API keys & secrets (Redwood): we will provision scoped API keys for the POC (owner: Marissa) — target: Oct 11
- IP allowlist (BrightLeaf): provide your egress IPs for peering and API allowlist (owner: Tom) — target: Oct 10
- VPC peering (infra teams): exchange subnet/cidr & initiate peering; request for a test route and NAT config (owners: BrightLeaf infra + Redwood infra) — kickoff: Oct 12, target completion: Oct 18
- Smoke validation (joint): token auth + small inference runbook (owner: Karthik) — target: Oct 19

Blocking items we flagged in the MAP: signed DPA (BrightLeaf legal), and IP ranges for peering. If either slips we will move the acceptance date accordingly.

Attached: an editable checklist with step owners and a minimal peering template. I included a small curl snippet for scoped key usage in the checklist.

Please reply with confirmations against each owner/date above or propose alternate dates. I can follow up with a short 30m sync after we lock dates.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP-Onramp-Wireup-Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@brightleaf.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, BrightLeaf Health - Platform Ops <ops@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Onramp wiring & POC infra gating — API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Thanks Grace — this layout is helpful. Quick confirmations and questions: 
- Org & billing: I'll create the evaluation org and invite redwood-poc@redwood.com by Oct 7 (we're on an internal approval chain but I'll nudge).
- IP allowlist: Ops can provide our egress ranges; I expect to have that by Oct 9, but if approvals slow we'll push one day. Do you need both IPv4 and IPv6? We primarily use IPv4 for the evaluation cluster.
- VPC peering: ops will need your peering template (subnet/cidr examples) and a short list of ports/protocols required. I see you attached a template — thanks. Can you confirm whether we need mutable routes or only static peering?
- DPA: Legal flagged minor data-retention language; our legal will send a redline by EOD Oct 6. Is a signed DPA required before we exchange API keys?

Also — for the scoped keys, can you confirm the token TTL you'd suggest for the POC (short lived, ideally 12h for testing)?

Tom
Tom Nguyen
Director, Platform Ops — BrightLeaf Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@brightleaf.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP: Onramp wiring & POC infra gating — API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Tom — great questions, answered inline: 
- IPv4 only is fine for the POC.
- Peering: our preferred pattern is a route-based peering with static routes on both sides so you can test without NAT translation. If you require NAT for egress we can support that from our side but it adds one step. I'll paste the required ports below: 443 (HTTPS to inference endpoints), 8443 (optional for observability proxy), and 22 (for controlled bastion access during setup) — default: 443 only.
- DPA: signed DPA is a precondition for production keys; for POC we can issue limited-scope keys while legal completes the DPA if your legal approves a provisional access letter. If you'd prefer, we can wait for the signed DPA — let us know.
- Token TTL: 12 hours is good for testing. We'll also provide a rotation script for your team in the checklist.

Action items I've taken:
- I attached a small peering snippet (poe-vpc-peering-template.txt) and populated the checklist with owners/dates per Grace's email.
- I'll provision a scoped API key once we confirm the org invite (Grace, if you see the invite please accept so I can create the key).

Next steps: Tom -> confirm org invite and IP ranges by Oct 9; Redwood (Marissa/Grace) -> provision key and share rotation script by Oct 11; Joint -> peering kickoff Oct 12. If we stay on this cadence, acceptance smoke tests on Oct 19 are realistic.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: poe-vpc-peering-template.txt (text)]
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@brightleaf.com>

- Org invite sent and accepted (I invited redwood-poc@redwood.com earlier today).
- Egress IPv4 ranges attached in a separate secure ticket (ops-#8423) — please let me know if you need CIDR expansion.
- Legal will send DPA redline by EOD Oct 6; provisional access letter OK for now to proceed with scoped key if you agree.

I'll schedule a 30m sync for Oct 13 (post-infra kickoff) to review peering progress and smoke plan. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Tom
